title: Keep the attempt, require a fresh correction
statement: After a wrong answer, keep the attempt visible, diagnose its misconception, and pass only the learner's own fresh correction, never an auto-filled answer or a repeated stale selection.
detail: Three rule sets for the reading courses agree. A lesson-acceptance checklist asks that a wrong answer preserve the attempt, diagnose the misconception and require a fresh correction; a Grade 5 teaching-flow release lists preserved wrong work, misconception-specific repair and a required fresh correction among what it proves at source and test level; and a course-experience preflight's outcome rule has feedback diagnose the submitted response, preserve work, withhold hints until an attempt and require correction or retry. None of them records an effect on learning.
against: A draft acceptance ladder for written answers offers one retry and then lets the student proceed anyway, queuing the attempt for review (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/scripts/lane-tools/drafts/m5-acceptance-rules.md`, lines 77-78), and another rule on record gives the answer after two tries. Two other builds release or settle after two tries instead. The lesson engine's evidence hunt and debate "now release after two tries" (`g9/transformer/v02/QA.md`, line 141), and a Grade 3 sample player settles graded items on the second try and records the miss separately: "It always completes by attempt 2 whether or not the child fixed the answer" (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/CONTENT-SCHEMA.md`, line 326).
